messages:
Alex: Quick heads-up — I'm prototyping a small console modal called "Model Cost Breakdown" that shows per-model effective token cost after amortized cache savings. Want quick sanity check before I wire the backend + console. TL;DR: show raw token cost, cache credits applied, sampling window, and a toggle to view per-route vs per-tenant amortization. Sketch + API below.

Alex: API sketch:
```http
POST /api/v1/console/cost_breakdown
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "model_id": "mix-13b",
  "start": "2026-03-10T00:00:00Z",
  "end": "2026-03-17T00:00:00Z",
  "sampling_rate": 0.01,
  "include_cache_credits": true,
  "amortization": "session" // options: session, route, tenant
}
```

Mira: Love the idea. A couple telemetry notes: we need an event `console.cost_breakdown.request` with fields `model_id, sampling_rate, amortization, probe_id` so we can correlate UI trials with eval sets. Also add `cache_before_tokens` / `cache_after_tokens` in the response schema.

Dan: Question: how do we avoid double-counting cache savings when the same prefix was prefetched by two tenants (shared prefetch pool)? If we just naively sum credits per-request we'll overshoot.

Sophia: Agree with Dan. We should carry a `prefetch_origin_id` and a lineage tag per cached item, then when attributing credits run a dedupe step by `lineage_id` and policy (first-touch vs weighted). Prefer first-touch for a start.

Evan: Per-request breakdown at query-time is going to be expensive on production telemetry. Suggest we build a small materialized table `mv_model_effective_cost_v1` that pre-aggregates:
```sql
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW mv_model_effective_cost_v1 AS
SELECT model_id, amort_window, date_trunc('hour', ts) as hour,
  sum(raw_tokens) as raw_tokens,
  sum(cache_saved_tokens) as cache_saved_tokens,
  sum(cost_before) as cost_before,
  sum(cost_after) as cost_after
FROM invocation_telemetry
WHERE ts > now() - interval '30 days'
GROUP BY model_id, amort_window, hour;
```
Update cadence could be 5m; then UI queries are cheap.

Alex: Good call. We still need a way to inspect raw samples for debugging and regressions though (the modal should link to a sampled raw-log view).

Mira: For sampling bias — if we use 1% sampling for UI, weight the sampled rows by `1 / sampling_rate` in the UI calculation. That should be good enough for a first pass. Also add a %uncertainty number computed by bootstrap on the sample.

Dan: If we do first-touch dedupe, we must record the `tenant_id` that owned the prefetch credit. Also warn in the modal that cross-tenant shared pools will show "apportioned" savings. UX should surface that caveat.

Sophia: UX nit: add a small toggle for "Show amortization policy" that expands text explaining session vs route vs tenant. Keeps the default clean.

Evan: Also: cache credits need a provenance column in the MV: `credit_policy, lineage_count` so we can debug when credits are large.

Alex: Plan then: I'll wire the console modal UI + call the MV endpoint. Evan — can you prototype the MV and a sample query? Mira — you'll own the telemetry event names and schema. Sophia/Dan — can you draft the dedupe policy text for the modal? I'll open a draft PR tomorrow. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy-checker: preflight lint passed for branch alex/model-cost-modal — canary gate queued.

Mira: acked. I'll add the event contract to the telemetry repo and paste the proto in the PR. :white_check_mark:

Evan: I'll spin up a small job that populates `mv_model_effective_cost_v1` and share the sample queries by EOD.

Dan: I'll draft the dedupe/first-touch wording and an edgecase note about shared prefetch pools.

Sophia: I'll mock the toggle copy and a short hover tooltip explaining uncertainty.

Alex: Thanks team — will link the PR here when it's ready.
